title: Dave's legacy: the Wilton library archive and the Brubeck News
summary: They discuss Dave's death ten years ago, the archive at the Wilton library, Richard Blumenthal's ribbon cutting and the Brubeck News.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: That’s great. Well I’ve just enjoyed so much talking to you both. And it’s hard to imagine that Dave passed away just about ten years ago.
That’s really hard to imagine that it’s been ten years. Crazy.
I’m pleased to hear that the library in Wilton is becoming or has become a home for —

Yeah. We were really thrilled that, and surprised, that at a time when he may have had a vote that could save democracy in America he — that was canceled for a couple of days so he came up and Richard Blumenthal did the ribbon cutting. Our state senator. And when we met him I just, you know, you don’t know what his background is. The first thing he says, he says, “We grew up in a classical household” the Blumenthal household, “and my brother and I, our big rebellion is we’d go out and buy your dad’s records.” So I knew like Obama and Clinton, you know we had someone that actually got it, that was glad to be there. And that was a wonderful thing.

Well the fact that you’re doing this and you have the Brubeck News going on, which I just read this morning, it’s terrific and I thank you for doing it. It’s really important. And even though it was delayed for a year and a half I guess, it’s all good.

It is all good and I’ve got to say that like the manifestation of that Brubeck News thing that you read wouldn’t happen if it weren’t for my wife working tirelessly on this. You know she was very close to Dave and Iola and she helped them with a lot of stuff, and that’s sort of what she does — a lot to keep us going too so I’m very grateful for that.
